title: Two Tiny Coins
objective: Children will hear the story of the poor widow who put two tiny coins into the Temple treasury, and learn that Jesus called her gift the biggest of all because she gave everything she had. They will count to two, compare *many* and *two*, and think of something they could give to God and to others.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Even a tiny gift is big to Jesus when we give with all our heart.

items.text: count the widow’s two coins, and tell *many* coins from *two*
items.question: count the widow’s coins?

items.text: say, in your own words, why Jesus called her two tiny coins the biggest gift
items.question: say why her tiny gift was the biggest?
items.screen: say why her tiny gift was the biggest

items.text: name one thing you could give to God or to others: a thing, some time or a kindness
items.question: name a gift you could give?
items.screen: name a gift I could give

materials: A big handful of coins and **two** pennies, kept apart
A bowl or basket to be the Temple treasury
The *Show your class* page (page 3), projected or printed
Crayons, including brown, and the differentiated handouts
questions: How many coins can you see? Let’s count them together.
Are these coins big or tiny?
The rich people gave lots of coins. Why did Jesus say the widow gave the most?
What could *you* give to God, or to someone who needs it?
connection: **Visit the exhibition:** find the Widow’s Mite in Case 7, *Ministry and Passion*. Count the coins together — there are two.
**Virtual visit:** in *Hands of History*, the children can meet the widow and see her hands holding the coins.

steps.title: Many coins, two coins
script: Sit in a circle with the bowl in the middle. Drop the big handful of coins in, one noisy handful at a time. Then, quietly, drop in the two pennies. Ask: *“Who gave more?”* Most children will point to the big handful. Say: *“Jesus watched people doing just this. And he said something surprising.”*

steps.purpose: Feel the difference between many coins and two, before the story turns it upside down.
students: Watch the coins go into the bowl.

steps.title: The poor widow
script: Explain that a widow is a woman whose husband has died. In Jesus’ time a widow often had very little. Tell the story simply: Jesus sat near the place in the Temple where people put their money for God. Many rich people put in lots of coins. Then a poor widow came. She put in two tiny coins. That was all she had.

verse.text: A poor widow came and put in two very small copper coins, worth only a few cents. Jesus said: she gave more than all the others.

screen.alt: The poor widow at the Temple, wrapped in a shawl, her hands held together

steps.purpose: Meet the widow, and hear what she gave.
students: How many coins did she give?

steps.title: What Jesus said
script: Jesus called his friends over. He told them that the widow had given more than everyone else. The others gave what they had left over; she gave everything. Read the passage aloud:

verse.text: Jesus sat down opposite the place where the offerings were put and watched the crowd putting their money into the temple treasury. Many rich people threw in large amounts. But a poor widow came and put in two very small copper coins, worth only a few pence. Calling his disciples to him, Jesus said, ‘Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all the others. They all gave out of their wealth; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything — all she had to live on.’

screen.alt: The widow’s cupped hands, holding her two tiny coins

steps.purpose: Hear Jesus’ surprising answer: the widow gave the most.

steps.title: Real coins from Jesus’ time
script: Show the two coins on page 3. These are real coins, very old, the same kind the widow gave. The exhibition shows **two** because the Gospel says two. Let children hold up two fingers, then cup their hands like the widow’s hands in the picture. Ask: *“Are they big or tiny? What color are they?”*

steps.purpose: See and count real coins of the kind the widow gave.
students: Count them. Hold up two fingers.

steps.title: Your handout
script: Each child works on a handout. All three show the same two coins and the same question: which was the biggest gift?

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Picture-led. Count the coins and circle the number, follow the dotted line from the coins to the widow’s hands, circle the biggest gift, color the two coins, trace *GIVE*.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: A little writing. Circle the number, draw a line from the coins to the hands, circle the biggest gift, copy *GIVE* under a model, then draw a gift of their own.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Draw and tell. Circle the biggest gift and say why, draw something they could give that matters to them, then tell a grown-up about it or write a few words.

steps.purpose: Count, compare and give on paper, at the right level for each child.
students: Which gift was the biggest? Find it on your page.

steps.title: Look back
script: Put the questions on the screen. For each one, the children show a thumb up, sideways or down: *“Can you now count the widow’s coins? Can you say why her tiny gift was the biggest? Can you name a gift you could give?”*

screen.hint: Show me: thumb up, sideways or down.

steps.title: Look back and share
script: Then say: *“The widow gave everything she had. Hold out your cupped hands. Tell a partner one thing you could share with someone today: a thing, some time, or a kindness.”*

screen.question: The widow gave everything she had. Hold out your cupped hands. Tell a partner one thing you could share with someone today: a thing, some time, or a kindness.

steps.purpose: Close with open hands, like the widow: name something to share today.
students: Hold out your cupped hands, like the widow.
Tell a partner one thing you could share today.

steps.title: Closing prayer (faith-based option)
script: **Faith-based option:** pray together, a line at a time: *“Dear Jesus, the widow gave you all she had. Help me to give you my heart, and to share with others. Amen.”*

steps.purpose: For faith schools: give the lesson back to God with open hands, like the widow.
students: Hold out your cupped hands, like the widow.
